📖 Instructions

Step-by-step tutorials for getting started with every part of the app.

🚀 1. Create your first exercise
  1. Click ➕ Create New Exercise in the sidebar, or pick a type from the tabs (Word Order, Flashcard, Test, etc.).
  2. Fill in the title and content for the exercise. Add students on the Students page first if you want this exercise to award points.
  3. Click Generate/Create — the file downloads straight to your device. Send it to students however you like (email, chat, USB, etc.). Students open it and type their student ID to begin.
👥 2. Add students & give them IDs
  1. Go to Students in the sidebar.
  2. Type a student's name and a unique ID (e.g. their student number), then click Add Student.
  3. Every ID must be different — this is what students type into an exercise instead of a name.
  4. You can remove a student any time; it won't delete their point history, just hide them from the leaderboard.
🏆 3. Points & the leaderboard
  1. When creating a Word Order, Make a Word, Flashcard, Spelling, or Test exercise, set how many points it's worth.
  2. When a student finishes and types their ID, points are added automatically — once per student per file.
  3. Open Points & Rewards to see the live leaderboard, or click ⬇ Download Shareable Leaderboard to send students a file that updates live on their end too.
  4. Tap the + / − next to any student to give or take bonus points yourself.
📊 4. Check results
  1. Results upload automatically the moment a student finishes an exercise (they need internet at that moment).
  2. Go to Results, then upload the exercise file itself (yours, or one a student sends back) — its results load automatically.
  3. Or open My Exercises and click 📊 View Results next to any exercise you've created — no upload needed.
  4. No internet when a student finished? They still get a downloaded results file you can import manually from the Results page.
📁 5. Manage your exercises
  1. My Exercises lists everything you've created in this browser.
  2. 🚫 Disable Points stops a specific file from ever awarding points again — students can still do the exercise, they just won't earn anything.
  3. 🗑 Delete permanently removes it from this list (the downloaded file and its results aren't affected).
⚙️ 6. Personalize your account
  1. Open Settings to switch between Day and Night mode.
  2. Set your own name — it appears whenever you give bonus points (e.g. "Bonus: By Teacher Toxirjon").
  3. Upload a profile picture — it shows in the sidebar.
Exercise-by-exercise tutorials
🧩Word Order
How to use

Type each full sentence normally — capital letter at the start, ending punctuation is optional. The app scrambles the words automatically, so you don't need to do anything else. Add at least 2 sentences, then set a points value if you want this exercise to award points. Click Create to download the file.

How it works

Students open the file, type their student ID, and see each sentence broken into scrambled word tiles. They drag the tiles into the correct order. Every sentence must be completed before the exercise finishes.

How marking works

A sentence only counts as correct once every word is in the exact right order (spelling of the words themselves doesn't matter, just their order). The score builds up per sentence completed, and the final certificate shows the score and time taken.

🧱Make a Word
How to use

Type single words with no spaces — e.g. "kitchen", "bookcase". Any spaces you type inside an entry are removed automatically before the puzzle is built. Add at least 2 words, then set a points value if you want it to award points, then click Create.

How it works

Students see each word's letters scrambled into tiles and drag them, one at a time, into empty slots to spell the word correctly.

How marking works

A word only counts as done once every letter sits in the right slot. There's no penalty for trying a letter in the wrong slot — students can keep adjusting until it's correct, and the score is based on how many words they complete.

🗂️Flashcard
How to use

Add word / translation pairs. Pick a design: grouped flashcards with a short quiz after each group, or the full-screen "car game" (needs at least 4 words so every question has three different wrong options to dodge). Set a points value if you want it to award points.

How it works

In the grouped design, students flip through the cards for one group, then answer a quick multiple-choice check on that group before the next group unlocks — direction (word→translation or the reverse) and quiz style are up to you. In the car game, the car drives itself down a lane while a word and three possible meanings sit at the top; students steer into the lane with the right answer before it reaches them.

How marking works

Each correct group-quiz answer builds the score; you can choose whether a wrong answer costs progress or just gets asked again. In the car game, picking the right lane keeps the run going — a wrong pick costs a life depending on the speed mode you chose.

🎬Presentation
How to use

Add as many slides as you like. On each slide, add text or image blocks, drag them anywhere on the canvas, and style each one on its own — nothing you change on one slide affects another. There's no student ID or points step here, since a presentation isn't something students complete or get scored on.

How it works

Students (or you, presenting on your own screen) click through the slides at their own pace. It behaves like a simple slideshow file that works fully offline once downloaded.

How marking works

Presentations aren't marked or scored — there's no certificate, no results, and nothing uploads anywhere. They're purely for showing content, not for testing it.

🗣️Pronunciation
How to use

Type only the words — the app works out pronunciation info for you automatically as you type. Pressing "Look up real pronunciations online" swaps those for the real dictionary version (needs internet, and only affects this editor — the downloaded file always works offline for the actual practice). Choose flashcard-style practice or the rocket game, and set a pass score and number of tries.

How it works

Students say each word out loud into their microphone, and the browser's built-in speech recognition compares what it heard to the target word. In the rocket game design, a word only lets them move forward once it's been said well enough, based on the pass score and tries you set.

How marking works

Only the browser's first guess counts, and how confident it was counts too — so saying a word badly no longer scores 100%. A different word than expected shows the wrong sounds in red; the right word said unclearly shows in amber with a lower score. Browser speech recognition still can't hear every small accent difference, so treat the percentage as a guide, not an exam mark. The microphone is only asked for once, on the very first screen — after that it stays on and never interrupts the lesson (opening the file from a shared web link, rather than straight from Downloads, keeps that permission to a single "Allow"). Students need Google Chrome or Edge, a microphone, and internet while speaking.

🔤Spelling
How to use

Type a correctly spelled word and three convincing wrong spellings are written for you automatically — a missing or extra double letter, a swapped quiet vowel, or a mixed-up ending. Add at least 2 words, then set a points value if you want it to award points, then click Create.

How it works

Students see all four spellings shuffled together and pick the one that's correct. A voice button can read the word aloud first if you've turned that on.

How marking works

Every correct pick adds to the score; there's no penalty for a wrong pick, they simply try again. Full marks come from picking the correct spelling across every word in the set.

📝Test
How to use

Type a full sentence, then click the one word that should be hidden — believable wrong options (other grammatical forms of that same word, like a different tense) are written for you automatically. Add at least 2 finished sentences, then set a points value if you want it to award points.

How it works

Students see the sentence with your chosen word blanked out, and pick the correct word from the shuffled options to fill the gap.

How marking works

Every correctly filled gap adds to the score. The final certificate shows the score out of the total number of sentences in the test.

✍️Sentences
How to use

Give a title and, optionally, a list of words — one sentence-space is created per word, and each must be used in its sentence. If you leave the words blank, write instructions instead (e.g. "Write sentences using Past Simple") and choose how many sentences students should write about anything they like.

How it works

Students see a light blue box for each sentence, labeled with the word they need to use if you gave one, or your general instruction if you didn't. They type their sentences and press Submit.

How marking works

If you gave specific words, the system checks each sentence actually contains its word before letting the student submit, highlighting any that don't. You can read every student's actual sentences afterward from the Results tab.

📖Bidirectional Language
How to use

Paste in an English reading passage (leave a blank line between paragraphs), choose the language to translate into, then hit "Split into sentences." Use "Auto-translate all" to fill in a first-pass translation, then read through and fix anything that needs it — the free translation service isn't perfect, and you can always edit any sentence by hand before creating the file.

How it works

Students see the English text on one side and your translation on the other, split into matching paragraphs and sentences. Hovering or tapping any sentence highlights it — and its matching pair — on both sides at once. Clicking any English word opens a lookup with its definition, pronunciation, and a translation of just that word. A translator tool and a notepad are also built in.

How marking works

There's nothing to answer right or wrong — this is a reading exercise, and it doesn't award points. Their notes (if they wrote any) are downloaded as a PDF and sent to you, viewable from Results.

🎬English Content
How to use

Give it a title and paste a video link — YouTube, Vimeo, Google Drive share links, and direct video-file links all work, auto-detected. Optionally set a 4-digit class code.

How it works

Students see the video on the left and a notes area on the right (they can drag the divider, down to a 50/50 split). On phones it stacks with the video on top. Pressing Finish downloads their notes as a PDF.

How marking works

This doesn't award points — it's a watch-and-note-taking activity. Their notes are sent to you and viewable from the Results tab.

🎧Dictation
How to use

Give it a title and paste a direct link to an audio file. Choose Free dictation (students type everything they hear, and you provide the correct transcript for grading) or Fill in the blanks (you paste the transcript and mark words to blank out by wrapping them in *asterisks*, like "The cat sat on the *mat*").

How it works

The audio player sits at the top of the screen on every device, with a night/day mode toggle. Students listen and write, then press Submit in the bottom-right.

How marking works

Grading is automatic. In Free dictation, each word is compared against your reference text — students see exactly which words were correct, which were wrong (with the right word shown), and which were missing, plus an overall percentage. In Fill in the blanks, each blank is checked against the word you marked. Their checked results are viewable from the Results tab.
